slides.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
slides.highlight: SocietyBench evaluates the ability of LLM agents to forecast social events using counterfactual timelines, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: SocietyBench evaluates LLM forecasting of social events using anonymized, counterfactual timelines to prevent pre-training memory recall.
card.key_idea: Real social events are transformed into counterfactual worlds via entity substitution and date shifting, then scored on probability calibration and temporal accuracy.
card.evaluation: Six frontier LLMs, three agent frameworks, and two heuristics were tested on five heterogeneous events; GPT-5.5 performed best (75.0/100).
card.limitation: High per-event score variance (up to 21.4 points) makes single-event evaluations unreliable for comparing model performance.

slides.title: Humanoid Companion Robot Market Projected to Reach US$1.1bn by 2030
slides.highlight: The rising demand for caregiving and emotional support is driving the humanoid companion robot market. This trend aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making
slides.tldr: SOCIAL SIMULATION ENGINE FOR HIGH-STAKES DECISION-MAKING
slides.highlight: WOPR provides a verifiable rules engine for social simulations of collective command-and-control systems, supporting the societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: WOPR is a social-simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making via a verifiable rules engine.
card.key_idea: A deterministic, replay-validated engine using a decision-point contract, a four-rung communication 'press ladder', and four command-and-control archetypes to simulate organizational military decisions.
card.evaluation: Verified via a 240-game sweep confirming seeded outcomes are preserved across engine changes; instantiated using the card game Nuclear War.
card.limitation: Early-stage work; lacks controlled studies, large-scale press mode evaluation, and automated enforcement of agent commitments.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Design guidance for using social robots to assess wellbeing in children with diverse communication needs.
card.key_idea: Used design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to identify inclusive, ethical requirements for robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with DLD and forced migration backgrounds.
card.evaluation: Qualitative thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across two specific vulnerable child populations.
card.limitation: The study is a qualitative design phase; it does not include direct testing or validation with children.

slides.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics
slides.highlight: TIDES provides longitudinal data on multi-party interactions and emergent roles, supporting HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid team states and group norms.

card.one_liner: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of university team meetings for modeling multi-party social dynamics.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 75,971 utterances with socio-structural annotations (interaction types, emergent roles, development stages) used to fine-tune LLMs for next-speaker and next-intention prediction.
card.evaluation: Tested on TIDES and AMI Meeting Corpus; fine-tuning improved next-speaker prediction by 13.8pp over bigram baseline and matched proprietary zero-shot models.
card.limitation: Improved structural prediction did not translate to more natural or coherent utterance generation in human evaluations.

slides.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
slides.tldr: HYBRID ATTENTION ESTIMATION FOR ADAPTIVE HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline combining geometric and semantic perception to regulate adaptive interaction behaviors in a robotic head, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A hybrid attention-estimation pipeline for an expressive robotic head to enable adaptive human-robot interaction behaviors.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast geometric perception layer (MediaPipe) for real-time state regulation with a VLM-based semantic observer (LLaVA-Phi3) for contextual attention labeling via a finite state machine.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants (40 trials). Results showed 100% interaction start reliability and successful adaptive pausing/resuming in distraction scenarios.
card.limitation: Controlled experimental setup, small participant sample, and lack of manual frame-level ground truth for attention labels.

slides.title: Google Unveils Gemini Robotics 2: Humanoid Robots Collaborate to Tidy Rooms
slides.highlight: Google's Gemini Robotics 2 demonstrates humanoid robots collaborating to tidy rooms, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: When AI Joins the Team! A Model of How AI Adoption Relates To Social Patterns in Software Engineering Teams
slides.tldr: AI ADOPTION AND SOCIAL PATTERNS IN SOFTWARE TEAMS
slides.highlight: This research examines how AI adoption influences social dynamics and communication quality in teams, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AI adoption reduces community smells through different mechanisms depending on whether the work involves specialization or coordination.
card.key_idea: Using PLS-SEM grounded in Transactive Memory Systems theory, the study models AI's impact on social anti-patterns via specialization-oriented and coordination-oriented human-human interactions.
card.evaluation: Survey data from 152 software professionals; validated via expert surveys, Exploratory Factor Analysis, and five PLS-SEM structural models.
card.limitation: The study relies on developers' perceptions of community smells rather than direct technical measurements of social anti-patterns.

slides.title: VISA: A Structured Description Protocol for Agent-Based Simulation Models Towards Machine Reproducibility
slides.tldr: STRUCTURED PROTOCOL FOR MACHINE-REPRODUCIBLE AGENT-BASED MODELS
slides.highlight: VISA introduces a symbol-based description protocol and LLM-executable skills to make agent-based models machine-parseable and unambiguous. This supports MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation by improving the reproducibility and transparency of agent models.

card.one_liner: VISA is a structured, symbol-based description protocol designed to make agent-based models machine-reproducible.
card.key_idea: It specifies models via eight interconnected tables (four agent-level, four model-level) using mathematical notation and nineteen consistency rules to ensure unambiguous, machine-parseable specifications.
card.evaluation: Validated on three external ABMs; successfully reproduced two cross-language (NetLogo to Python) and captured one industrial AnyLogic model, identifying specific proprietary blockers.
card.limitation: Reproduction can still be blocked by proprietary libraries or unavailable data, though VISA explicitly localizes and names these dependencies.

slides.title: Beyond Feeling Better: Capability-Sustaining Emotional Dialogue as a Longitudinal Research Paradigm
slides.highlight: This work proposes a paradigm for emotional dialogue that sustains user capacities for emotion regulation and social connection, contributing to HyECHO's focus on engagement and social perception.

card.one_liner: Proposes CSED, a longitudinal paradigm for emotional dialogue focusing on sustaining user capabilities over time.
card.key_idea: Shifts focus from immediate relief to sustaining emotion regulation, coping, autonomy, and social connection via six design commitments and a four-timescale evaluation framework.
card.evaluation: Literature audit of 91 papers and function-coding of 300 ESConv turns; found 95% of system-building papers are relief-oriented with no longitudinal evaluation.
card.limitation: Relies on latent state proxies; longitudinal measurement introduces privacy risks and potential conflicts between immediate relief and long-term capability.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC GOVERNANCE FOR VERIFIABLE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework to bridge neural reasoning with deterministic governance for verifiable AI agents, supporting the MIMIC goal of simulating harmonious human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A decentralized governance framework using neuro-symbolic profiles and blockchain to verify AI agent capabilities and compliance.
card.key_idea: Binds LLM agents to symbolic domain ontologies via Verifiable Credentials, using blockchain smart contracts for identity verification, dynamic role binding, and immutable interaction logging.
card.evaluation: Tested with a healthcare prototype (3 agents) across 42 cases; achieved 100% attack detection and O(1) verification complexity relative to ecosystem size.
card.limitation: Focuses on admission governance and provenance; does not verify the actual quality or correctness of the agent's clinical recommendations.

slides.title: StreamTalk: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Key-Pose Anchoring
slides.highlight: StreamTalk introduces a closed-loop framework for real-time 3D gesture generation that reduces long-horizon drift, supporting the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: StreamTalk prevents long-term motion drift in streaming co-speech gestures using a closed-loop retrieval-based anchoring framework.
card.key_idea: A generate-retrieve-refine cycle uses a speaker-specific database to provide destination key-pose anchors, supported by Stochastic Anchor Masking (SAM) and a part-aware DiT architecture.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT2 benchmark using FGD, BC, and user studies; achieved state-of-the-art motion quality and real-time performance (76 FPS).

slides.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTRIC EMBODIED INTELLIGENCE FOR WEARABLE ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This review introduces the PCAA framework for soft wearable robots, emphasizing the integration of sensing and adaptive cognition to improve human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: A review proposing the HCEI framework to shift soft wearable robotics toward human-centric, intelligent systems.
card.key_idea: The Perception-Cognition-Actuation-Augmentation (PCAA) framework prioritizes sensing and cognition over actuators to enable adaptive, personalized human-robot coupling.

slides.title: Learning Social Robot Navigation By Sensing Human Legs
slides.tldr: SOCIAL ROBOT NAVIGATION VIA LEG SENSING
slides.highlight: Introduces CALF, a neural architecture that interprets leg motion from LiDAR scans to improve social compliance in robot navigation, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: CALF enables social robot navigation by interpreting human leg dynamics from ankle-height 2D LiDAR scans.
card.key_idea: A hybrid architecture combining 1D-CNNs, temporal self-attention, and MLP, trained via DRL in LegNav, a simulator featuring a novel Non-Slip Gait model for realistic leg dynamics.
card.evaluation: Compared against classical and RL baselines in LegNav and validated via zero-shot deployment on a TurtleBot 4; results showed smooth, socially compliant trajectories.
